headline: Verify Washington Discover Pass Requirements
reservation: Most Washington-side trailheads require a Discover Pass for vehicle parking, which must be purchased in advance or at automated stations where available. Popular spots like Dog Mountain may require additional seasonal permits for weekend hiking to manage capacity. Always check Washington State Parks and USFS websites for changing permit mandates before arrival.

days.title: Volcanic Heights and River History

stops.name: Beacon Rock State Park
stops.detail: Ascend the switchback trail of this massive basalt monolith for expansive views of the river; check for seasonal raptor nesting closures.

stops.name: Columbia Gorge Museum
stops.detail: Explore regional heritage and see a working steam traction engine in the heart of Stevenson.

days.driving: Allow 1–2 hours; SR-14 is a primary freight corridor with moderate curves.
days.note: The Beacon Rock summit trail involves narrow boardwalks and steep drop-offs.

days.title: Wildflowers and Wetland Birds

stops.name: Steigerwald Lake National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Walk the levee trails to observe migratory waterfowl and enjoy the quiet transition from urban to gorge landscapes.

stops.name: Catherine Creek
stops.detail: Explore the interpretive trails known for spring wildflowers and views of the river's south wall.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; conditions vary based on local wind speeds.
days.note: Ticks are common in the tall grasses of Catherine Creek during spring and summer.

days.title: The High Desert Edge

stops.name: Coyote Wall
stops.detail: Hike the dramatic cliffs for views of the Syncline, keeping watch for mountain bikers on shared-use segments.

stops.name: Maryhill Stonehenge
stops.detail: Visit the full-scale replica of the English monument, serving as a memorial with commanding views of the eastern gorge.

stops.name: Maryhill Museum of Art
stops.detail: Examine world-class collections in a mansion perched on the cliffs; verify seasonal opening dates before visiting.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours for the round trip toward Maryhill; roads are open and exposed.
days.note: Maryhill is significantly drier; carry extra water as services are infrequent east of Lyle.

intel.title: Discover Pass Logistics
intel.text: Ensure your Discover Pass is clearly displayed at Beacon Rock to avoid fines. Some USFS trailheads require the Northwest Forest Pass instead.

intel.title: Gorge Shadows
intel.text: Signal is often lost near the tunnels on SR-14 and within the deep forest sections near Carson. Pre-load your navigation for the drive to Maryhill.

intel.title: Fuel Scarcity East
intel.text: Services are readily available in Stevenson and Bingen but become sparse as you head toward Maryhill. Fill up in White Salmon before heading to the eastern viewpoints.

intel.title: Wildflower Windows
intel.text: April and May are peak for Catherine Creek blooms, but the window varies annually by two weeks. Visit early in the day to beat the midday Gorge winds.

intel.title: Bridge Crossings
intel.text: The Hood River-White Salmon bridge and the Bridge of the Gods are tolled. Check for weight and height restrictions if operating a large RV.

plan.arrival: Fly into PDX, cross the Glenn Jackson Bridge, and take SR-14 East. Stop in Washougal for hiking supplies before the drive to Stevenson.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for SR-14; RVs should be cautious of narrow lanes and high winds near the Columbia River.
plan.goldenHour: Coyote Wall offers striking lighting at sunset, highlighting the dramatic basalt folds of the Syncline.
